title: Choosing between CP-SAT and a MIP solver

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A model orders 15 pump overhauls for one crew, each pair written as two big-M rows with M equal to the total of all overhaul days. After many branch-and-bound nodes, HiGHS has a good order but a best bound of almost 0. What makes the bound so weak?

options.text: the node limit stops HiGHS before it can solve a single LP
options.says: HiGHS solved LPs at thousands of nodes in the lesson's run, and its bound stayed near 0 throughout.

options.text: the bound cannot rise at all until HiGHS proves its order the best
options.says: The bound rises as branching fixes order variables; it is low because each fix moves it only a little.

options.text: the integer start days make the LP relaxation unsolvable
options.says: The LP relaxation drops integrality, start days included, and is solved at every node.

options.text: a fractional order variable lets every job start on day 0
options.says: Right: with each pair's binary at one half, both big-M rows hold with every start at day 0, so the relaxation sees no lateness.

questions.stem: A utility's ten-year plan has 3,000 projects with start-year binaries, one budget row per year and a few precedence rows, and its LP relaxation is within 0.1% of the integer optimum. Which solver should the team try first?

options.text: CP-SAT on one worker, since its search needs no LP relaxation at all
options.says: On GridCap medium's ten-year model one CP-SAT worker ended 3% from its bound, the worst of the three runs.

options.text: a MIP solver, since the LP relaxation already bounds it tightly
options.says: Right: a strong LP relaxation is what branch-and-bound uses; HiGHS ended closest to proven on the same kind of model.

options.text: CP-SAT on many workers, since a portfolio comes out ahead on large models
options.says: The 8-worker portfolio ended at 0.12% while HiGHS ended at 0.05%.

options.text: either one, since the two solvers end at the same gap on a linear model
options.says: The crew-order model is linear too, and the two solvers differed sharply on it.

origin.section: Large Models With Strong LP Bounds Favor a MIP Solver

questions.stem: A gas network model has a continuous flow on each pipe and a yes/no decision for each valve. A developer wants to write it directly with CP-SAT's `CpModel`. What does that API offer for the flows?

options.text: a float variable for each flow, made with `new_float_var`
options.says: CpModel's variable makers are new_bool_var, new_int_var and new_int_var_from_domain; there is no float variable.

options.text: a Boolean for each flow, read as open or closed
options.says: A Boolean has two values; a flow is an amount.

options.text: integer variables only; scale the flows or use MathOpt
options.says: Right: CpModel has integers only; scale the flows to whole units, or build the model in MathOpt.

options.text: an LP solve of the flows, with duals as an LP solver gives
options.says: CP-SAT reports a bound but no duals or reduced costs.

origin.section: Continuous Amounts Need MathOpt or Scaling
